searches.reason: Explore learned retention as an alternative to fixed recency weighting. A time-conditioned GRU could preserve durable interests while adapting to changing intent within one jointly trained model. First verify padding invariance; existing context-removal measurements remain confounded and do not justify discarding older history.

searches.reason: Investigate whether title and description supervision can distinguish specific interests from broad relatedness, especially in sparse histories. Seek lightweight text encoders trained from scratch and jointly integrated into one GRU recommender, using only supplied text and interactions. Text similarity alone cannot establish compatibility or current need.

searches.reason: Challenge whether strong separation against easy sampled negatives transfers to ranking among competitive candidates. Seek efficient sampled-softmax objectives and false-negative-aware hard-negative mining within a single GRU model. Compare against uniform BPR-max under matched sampling where possible, selecting only through the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10.
